material_items_for_expert_correction: External assurance wording implies assurance may have been obtained for Scope 1 and Scope 2. Given operational GHG records are flagged as not available, and the evidence package does not provide an assurance statement or scope details for the reporting period, this must be reframed to avoid implying assurance was obtained (eg, state the Bank does not obtain external assurance for this report; if assurance is obtained in future/elsewhere, specify location and scope).
minor_wording_for_editorial_review: “This report sets out … climate‑ and sustainability‑related financial disclosures.” (Fine, but could clarify that the report focuses primarily on climate, with broader sustainability only to the extent addressed, to avoid implying full S1 breadth.)
“These horizons are intended to be broadly consistent with the Bank’s internal strategic and risk planning cycles.” (Defensible; could be tightened to “are aligned to” only if evidenced.)

“The Bank seeks to describe the nature of the metrics and key limitations at a high level in the relevant sections of the report.” (Could be tightened to avoid implying this is consistently done unless confirmed in the core sections.)

data_limited_requirements: No separate climate-specific Board charter or terms of reference is disclosed.
No ESG & Sustainability Committee charter or formal terms of reference is disclosed.
No formal escalation thresholds or trigger-based escalation mechanics for climate-related risks are disclosed.
No formal process for assessing the adequacy of Board climate-related skills and competencies is disclosed.
No quantified Board-level trade-offs between climate objectives and other considerations are disclosed.
No formal policy document governing climate checks for major transactions is disclosed.
Committee names differ across 2022–2024 and the Bank does not disclose whether these are the same evolving committee or separate bodies.
Assurance boundary is clearly stated: limited assurance over Scope 1 and Scope 2 only; financed emissions and other Scope 3 are outside scope.
material_items_for_expert_correction: Overview: 'Eurolux Universal Bank AG integrates climate-related governance into its overall corporate governance framework.' This is broader than the evidence provided (which supports specific mechanisms—agenda coverage, committee existence/activity, semi-annual reporting, ERM integration flags, risk register use, transaction checks, remuneration linkages—but not an overarching integration into the full corporate governance framework). Reframe to describe the evidenced mechanisms without asserting enterprise-wide integration.

Board committees subsection: 'is involved in reviewing climate-related targets, methodologies and plans before they are submitted to the Board.' Evidence supports committee/board decisions on scenario methodology and transition plan endorsement, but does not evidence a standing pre-submission review role across targets/methodologies/plans as a defined process. Reframe to 'considered' or 'reviewed in 2024' rather than asserting an ongoing role.
minor_wording_for_editorial_review: Board role subsection: 'This trend indicates...' (agenda coverage and expertise trends). Consider neutral phrasing ('Climate-related topics appeared on the agenda in...') to avoid implying causality or qualitative conclusions beyond the metric.

Management subsection: 'Climate checks for major transactions are recorded as part of management processes.' Tighten to avoid implying a formalised process framework; evidence supports that checks occur, but not a formal mandatory policy.

Management subsection: 'The register also records mitigation actions at the risk level.' Supported by mitigation-action fields, but consider clarifying these are recorded actions rather than confirmed implemented controls.

data_limited_requirements: Upstream suppliers are assessed qualitatively, without separate quantified financial exposure.
The Bank does not currently disclose a detailed set of transition-plan assumptions and dependencies in this Strategy section beyond high-level descriptions.
The Bank does not currently disclose documented or quantified trade-off analysis for strategic decisions where climate-related risks and opportunities may interact with other objectives.

The Bank does not currently publish a separate, detailed business-model impact assessment that quantifies how climate-related factors may reshape its overall business model beyond portfolio and value-chain effects.

The Bank has not yet quantified the specific current-period impact of climate-related factors on individual financial statement line items (net interest income, fee income, impairment charges, capital ratios).

The Bank does not currently disclose a detailed mapping of climate-related risks and opportunities to specific future changes in financial position, performance and cash flows, nor planned dedicated sources of funding beyond general plans.
Scenario outputs are described as modelled estimates and not realised losses; resilience statements are scenario-specific and bounded.
Opportunity-related revenue and cost impacts are management estimates with a stated confidence level and not assured outcomes.
Targets are summarised; baseline details, interim milestones, validation bodies, gross/net status and planned use of carbon credits are not described.
material_items_for_expert_correction: “All three targets are currently assessed as on track …” (Target status is supported, but presenting ‘on track’ without stating that only a summary is disclosed can be read as a strong assurance-like claim; it should be explicitly bounded in the Strategy narrative that the assessment is based on internal tracking and that baseline/milestones/validation details are not disclosed in this section.)
minor_wording_for_editorial_review: “Dedicated climate-related capital and operating expenditure support implementation.” (Fine, but could be tightened to avoid implying ring-fenced budgets if not separately tracked as such.)

“The lending book is the primary transmission channel … complemented by actions in own operations and procurement.” (Supported directionally; could clarify that upstream procurement is assessed qualitatively.)
“Carbon price trajectories from international net-zero pathways …” (Tighten to the stated methodology: IEA NZE 2050 trajectory mapping, if that is the Bank’s approach.)

data_limited_requirements: The Bank does not currently disclose formal climate risk appetite thresholds, detailed climate risk policy documents or formal escalation thresholds and triggers for climate-related risks.

Detailed formal controls and procedures for climate-related risk management (including underwriting, collateral management, pricing, ECL estimation and day-to-day monitoring) are not documented for disclosure in this report.

Upstream climate-related risks linked to suppliers, service providers or funding sources are not separately identified or quantified in the climate risk register and are outside the scope of this report.
Internal operational climate-related risks are not recorded as separate entries in the climate risk register and are outside the scope of this report.
Methodologies for indicative financial impact estimates and linkage to financial statement line items are not disclosed; scenario outputs are modelled estimates subject to uncertainty.
material_items_for_expert_correction: “Mitigation actions … include … collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays …” and similar action statements are presented in places as if they are implemented controls/processes. The evidence supports that these are recorded mitigation actions in the register, but not that they are implemented as formalised, bank-wide day-to-day procedures. This needs consistent framing as ‘recorded actions’ rather than implying operational effectiveness or uniform application.
minor_wording_for_editorial_review: “The register provides a structured view of climate-related risks that could affect the Bank’s lending portfolios and related activities.” (Tighten to ‘lending and credit portfolios’ to match the register scope described elsewhere.)

“Scenario analysis is used as a forward-looking input…” (Good boundary; consider adding that it is applied to selected risks only, each linked in the register, to avoid any inference of portfolio-wide application.)

data_limited_requirements: Operational Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions are not disclosed for 2024 due to unavailability of detailed records.
No financed-emissions perimeter detail (asset class/sector/geography) is disclosed; no sector/asset class/geography disaggregation is provided.
Detailed calculation methodology, data quality assessments and significant assumptions are not described.
Metrics and targets/progress indicators have not been independently verified; target-record validation fields are not presented as assurance of current-year emissions or target achievement.
material_items_for_expert_correction: Implied coherence between the financed emissions intensity target baseline/milestones (20.0; 18.2; 15.8 tCO₂e/EURm) and the disclosed 2024 portfolio carbon intensity (1,154.81 tCO₂e/EURm). As drafted, stating the 2024 metric is used to monitor progress against that target is not credible without an explanation of differing definitions/perimeters/denominators or a correction of the target-record intensity units/values.
minor_wording_for_editorial_review: “focus on … medium- and long-term greenhouse gas reduction targets” (targets include 2030 and 2050; consider explicitly stating time horizons rather than qualitative labels).

“These loans include financing that supports low-carbon and climate-resilient activities” (define the green loan taxonomy/criteria or explicitly state that the classification methodology is not described in this report).
“provide a decision-useful overview” (acceptable, but could be softened given the stated methodology and disaggregation gaps).
